label: broken

unstated.what: Ufunc support for a dtype= keyword (np.positive(df, dtype=np.float32) must return a DataFrame with float32 dtypes); the instruction only mentions the out parameter
unstated.quote:
result = np.positive(df, dtype=np.float32)
    assert all(d == np.float32 for d in result.dtypes)

unstated.what: np.negative with out= must write into an int64 ndarray (sibling unary ufunc; same __array_ufunc__ out-handling fix covers it)
np.exp with out= writes to ndarray (sibling unary ufunc, same fix)
Ufunc must also honor a dtype keyword (np.positive(df, dtype=np.float32)) returning a DataFrame whose columns are cast to that dtype — no dtype kwarg behavior is mentioned in the issue.
unstated.quote:
result = np.positive(df, dtype=np.float32)
    assert all(d == np.float32 for d in result.dtypes)

unstated.what: Unary ufuncs np.exp and np.negative must write results into an out array — not named in the instruction (which only shows np.add), though same-family siblings fixed by the identical change.

Ufuncs applied to a DataFrame must honor the numpy `dtype` keyword, returning a DataFrame whose dtypes are the requested dtype (np.float32) — the instruction only mentions the `out` parameter, never `dtype`.
unstated.quote:
result = np.positive(df, dtype=np.float32)
    assert all(d == np.float32 for d in result.dtypes)

reasons: The instruction only describes the out= bug; the dtype= keyword behavior for ufuncs (float32 dtypes) is an extra semantic the instruction never mentions, so it is not inferable. The other ufunc/out cases (negative, exp) are covered by the same minimal __array_ufunc__ out fix.

The core out= fix for DataFrame ufuncs is covered and the unary siblings (exp/negative) fall out of the same change, but the test that a dtype kwarg is honored and cast into the resulting DataFrame's dtypes describes behavior nowhere stated in the instruction.

The instruction only describes fixing the `out` parameter for DataFrame ufunc dispatch; all out-related and preservation tests follow from that fix or guard existing behavior. The dtype-kwarg test requires extra semantics (dtype propagation to result dtypes) never mentioned in the issue, which a minimal out-fix would not implement.
